questions.quesText: In relational database design, which normal form eliminates transitive functional dependencies?
questions.explanation: A relation is in Third Normal Form (3NF) if it is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on the primary key.

questions.quesText: In SQL, the command used to remove all records from a table without logging individual row deletions is ____.
questions.explanation: The TRUNCATE command is a DDL operation that deallocates data pages rather than logging row deletions, making it much faster than DELETE.

questions.quesText: In ACID transaction properties, Atomicity ensures that either all operations of a transaction succeed, or none take effect.
questions.explanation: True. The all-or-nothing property of transactions is known as Atomicity.

questions.quesText: In computer architecture, the technique of fetching the next instruction while the current instruction is being executed is called:
questions.explanation: Instruction pipelining overlaps the execution phases of consecutive instructions to increase instruction throughput.

questions.quesText: The fastest and smallest memory unit located directly inside the CPU processor chip is called a ____.
questions.explanation: Registers reside directly on the processor core and provide the fastest data access times in the computer memory hierarchy.

questions.quesText: SRAM (Static RAM) requires periodic electrical refresh cycles to retain stored data.
questions.explanation: False. DRAM requires periodic refreshing because it stores charge in capacitors, whereas SRAM uses flip-flops and retains data as long as power is supplied without refresh cycles.

questions.quesText: Which algorithmic design paradigm does the 0/1 Knapsack problem typically use for an optimal polynomial-time solution?
questions.explanation: The 0/1 Knapsack problem exhibits overlapping subproblems and optimal substructure, making Dynamic Programming the standard approach to find the optimal solution in O(nW) pseudo-polynomial time.

questions.quesText: In algorithm analysis, the time complexity of Merge Sort in all cases (worst, average, and best) is ____.
questions.explanation: Merge sort divides the list into halves and merges them in linear time at each of the log n levels, resulting in O(n log n) time in all cases.

questions.quesText: Dijkstra's shortest path algorithm produces correct results even when the graph contains negative weight edges.
questions.explanation: False. Dijkstra's greedy approach fails on graphs with negative edge weights; the Bellman-Ford algorithm must be used instead.
